A free **310K-context** `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` entry for **OpenCode 2.x**, plus the plugin that
keeps multi-hour sessions from dying, drifting, or quietly getting dumber.

**Version:** v1.8.1 · **Status:** stable — 148/148 unit tests, the compaction/pruning core
live-verified on OpenCode 2.1.3 · **Cost:** $0 · **Scope:** one provider, one model id, nothing else
is touched.

```powershell
# Windows
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
bash install.sh
```

Then quit OpenCode completely, reopen it, and pick **flash 1047 - Super Free**. Details in

## Who this is for

- You use the **free** `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` model in OpenCode and a long task (an hour or
  more) ends with a dead session, an early compaction, a lost thread, or the model inventing work.
- You want the **biggest window you can actually use** — 310 000 tokens measured, not the 200 000
  the stock entry claims.
- You want a plugin that **never swaps your model** and never silently changes the answer quality.

## Who this is not for

- **Hard reasoning problems.** This is a free Flash-tier model. It is good at bulk edits, refactors,
  test loops and long mechanical work; it is not a frontier model and will lose to one on design
  questions. If that is the job, pay for a better model.
- **Low latency.** A long session costs 10–30 s per model step, and one user message can be ~11
  steps. See [Speed expectations](#speed-expectations).
- **Not OpenCode.** The provider block is OpenCode-specific and the plugin is an OpenCode 2.x plugin.

## This entry vs the stock entry

Same model id, same weights, same $0. The difference is two things: **the declared window** and
**the plugin that manages it**.

### The numbers

| | stock `opencode` entry | this entry |
|---|---|---|
| model id | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` | same |
| price | $0 | $0 |
| declared context | 200 000 | **310 000** |
| where the client compacts | ~170 000 (limit − 15%) | **263 500** (85%) |
| usable before compaction | ~170k | **~263k** |
| measured gateway wall | 319 123 accepted / 325 760 rejected | the same wall, kept in mind |
| output | 32 000 | 32 000 |
| reasoning variants | low / high / max | low / medium / high / max |
| calibrated size estimate | no (`chars / 3.6`) | **yes, per model** |
| old tool output trimmed | no | **yes, with a marker** |
| dead-stream retry | the turn ends | **retried, up to 7** |
| resume after a failed turn | no | **yes** |
| post-compaction anchor | no | **yes** |
| task saved on disk | no | **`.omo/goals/<sessionID>.md`** |
| model switching | — | **never** |

The 170 000 figure is not a defect of the model: the runtime compacts at `limit − max(15%, 16 000)`,
so a declared 200 000 costs ~93 000 tokens of working memory before the first summary. Declaring the
measured 310 000 is what buys those ~93 000 back.

### In a long session

| what happens | stock entry | this entry |
|---|---|---|
| a 200 000-character log lands in context | the next request is too big | the middle is elided with a marker, the turn survives |
| context reaches the compaction point | compacts at ~170k, early | compacts at 263.5k, with ~46k of headroom |
| the summary loses your wording | you re-explain | the goal file + the note carry your asks verbatim |
| after compaction | the session waits for you | one prompt continues the task, anchored on the goal |
| the stream dies at 90% | the turn fails | retried; pruned harder on the second failure |
| the summariser stream is truncated | compaction fails, the session stalls | backoff, then emergency trim: the session keeps working |
| context pressure | "keep replies short" | full quality, targeted reads, findings written down |
| the model itself | same quality per token | same quality per token |

### vs a paid model

| | this | a paid frontier model |
|---|---|---|
| cost | $0 | per token |
| window | 310k measured | usually 200k–1M, varies |
| hard reasoning | weaker | **stronger** |
| long mechanical work | **what it is for** | fine, but you pay |
| rate limits | shared free pool | your quota |

Practical split: use this for refactors, test loops, log hunting, migrations and anything long and
mechanical. Switch to a paid model when the problem is the thinking, not the typing.

## What it fixes

| symptom you have seen | cause | what this repo does |
|---|---|---|
| `400 context_length_exceeded` around 200k | the declared window is wrong | declares 310 000, measures real usage, calibrates per model |
| compaction fires every turn and fails | cooldown counted from the request, not the failure | backoff measured from the failure: 3 → 6 → 12 → 24 → 30 min |
| the session goes idle after compaction and waits for you | nothing continues the turn | auto-continue prompt + the goal file on disk |
| "the model forgot what I asked" | the summary paraphrased your requirements away | the compaction note carries your last four asks **verbatim**, and the goal file keeps a `## Requirements` section |
| after compaction it continues the wrong thing | an informational "у меня поиск запущен, просто чтобы ты знал" overwrote the goal | **one goal**: an addition goes to its own `## Additions` section and is quoted as context, never as the task |
| one reworded demand eats the task list | every message was appended as a new requirement | an extension **replaces** the old requirement (the longer version wins) instead of taking another slot |
| the model gets lazy in long chats | pressure notes said "keep replies short, avoid re-reading" | notes now say: full quality, verify, use targeted reads, record findings |
| a stream dies mid-answer (`ECONNRESET`) | the free gateway closes it | transport retry, force-prune on the second failure |
| the whole session dies at ~250k | the summariser stream gets truncated | emergency trim: old tool output and old text are cut, the session keeps working |
| it looks like the model is "hanging" | hidden reasoning + retries + many steps | visible: `compact-backoff` / `retry` / `ctx` lines in `.omo/logs/resilience.jsonl` |

## Speed expectations

Measured on a real 250k-token session: 96 user messages, 1 047 assistant steps, 1 093 tool calls.

| | |
|---|---|
| model calls per user message | ~11 |
| generation per step, median / p90 | 10.4 s / 30 s |
| total generation time in that session | ~4 hours |
| context re-sent per step | ~155 000 tokens (cached) |

A step costs roughly what the context costs, so a fresh chat answers in seconds while a 250k
session costs 10–30 s per step. The plugin makes long sessions **survivable**, not **fast**: it caps
the context at 310 000, trims old tool output and stops compaction from storming.

Two practical notes:

- **Start a new session for a new task.** That resets the per-step cost from ~155k tokens to a few
  thousand. It is the single biggest speed lever there is.
- **`high` vs `max` is not a speed lever.** Measured medians differ by under 10%; pick the variant on
  quality, not on speed.

## How a request flows

The plugin is three hooks and one event stream. Every mutation is applied to the **outgoing request
only**; the stored session is never rewritten.

```
 user prompt
     │
     ▼
 ┌─ session.context ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ 1. strip a pressure note left by a previous request           │
 │ 2. estimate size (ASCII 3.6 ch/tok, wide text 2.0 ch/tok)      │
 │ 3. used = estimate × cal        ratio = used / 310 000         │
 │ 4. clamp options.maxTokens so prompt + reply ≤ 318 000 − 4 000 │
 │ 5. prune stale tool output (≥ 70% of the window)               │
 │ 6. append one pressure note at the current level               │
 │ 7. record prevEst = size of what is actually about to be sent  │
 │ 8. if ratio ≥ 85% → session.compact()                          │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
     │
     ▼
   provider  ──(usage: input + cache.read + cache.write)──►  cal updated (EMA)
     │
     ▼
   session.idle / execution-failed  ──►  resume prompt, checkpoint, re-anchor
```

Why step 7 matters: the provider reports usage for the request that was **sent**. Recording
`prevEst` before pruning would make `cal = real / prevEst` shrink in proportion to the pruned share
(0.44 instead of 1.2 in the regression test), so every later decision would under-count and the 85%
trigger would fire far above the real ceiling. The estimate is therefore recorded after pruning, and
there is a dedicated test for it.

## Context policy

Thresholds are fractions of `contextLimit` (310 000 as shipped):

| level | value | tokens | what happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pruneSoft` | 70% | 217 000 | start eliding the middle of stale tool output |
| `warn` | 70% | 217 000 | note: work at full quality, prefer targeted reads, record findings |
| `compact` | **85%** | 263 500 | request compaction, then re-anchor |
| `hard` | 93% | 288 300 | last-resort note if compaction did not reduce usage |
| runtime auto | — | 270 000 | OpenCode's own compaction, kept as a safety net |

**The `buffer` contract.** OpenCode auto-compacts at `limit − max(15% of limit, 16 000)` = 263 500
by default, i.e. exactly where the plugin triggers. Setting `compaction.buffer: 40000` moves the
runtime to `310 000 − 40 000 = 270 000`, so the plugin compacts first and the runtime stays a
backstop below the real 319K wall.

**The `keep` contract.** `compaction.keep.tokens` and the plugin's `keep` **must be the same
number** (32 000 shipped). The runtime cannot summarise anything inside the keep window, so a
trigger below `keep` only produces `Nothing to compact yet`; the plugin detects that case and backs
off instead of asking again on every request.

Two invariants hold for any preset:

```
compact × limit  <  limit − buffer          (plugin triggers before the runtime)
keep            <  compact × limit          (there is something left to summarise)
```

Shipped: `263 500 < 270 000` ✔ and `32 000 < 263 500` ✔.

### Calibration, with numbers

One real sample arrives per completed step: `real = input + cache.read + cache.write`.

```
cal ← cal × (1 − w) + (real / prevEst) × w      w = 0.65 on a sharp shift, 0.4 otherwise
cal is clamped to [0.4, 2.5]
```

A first sample is taken raw (`calN = 0`), then smoothed. Guards: `prevEst ≥ 1 500`,
`real ≥ 1 000`, and `0.3 < real / prevEst < 3` — anything outside is a measurement artefact
(the step was retried, a tool returned early), not a calibration event. Samples are keyed by
assistant-message identity so parallel tool calls count once while a genuinely identical second
turn still counts.

### Pruning

Past `pruneSoft`, the middle of old tool results is replaced with head and tail plus an explicit
marker:

> `[omni-resilience] 41 233 chars were removed from the middle of this tool output by the client
> to protect the context window. You cannot see them - do not guess or reconstruct their contents.
> Re-run the tool with grep/offset/limit if you need that part again.`

At `compact` pressure the retained head/tail shrink further and only the last 6 tool results stay
intact. That is why a 200 000-character log does not have to end the session.

## Behaviour reference

| mechanism | policy |
|---|---|
| **retry transport** | `1200 ms × attempt`, capped at 8 000 ms; force-prune on the 2nd failure; give up on the 7th |
| **retry 5xx** | `700 + 400 × count`, capped at 2 500 ms; 45 s budget per episode |
| **retry 429** | `3000 × 2^(count−1) × 0.6`, capped at 15 000 ms; 60 s budget |
| **not retried** | 4xx other than 408/409/425/429, own stall interrupts, `provider.invalid-request` |
| **fatal** | 4xx naming the model as unavailable/unknown, auth, permission, 401/403, no-route |
| **never** | model switching, silent failover, rewriting stored messages |
| **resume** | after an exhausted turn, quotes your task, max 4 per message, 2-minute cooldown |
| **stall** | 15 min without an event, verified against server state, then interrupt → verify → resume |
| **checkpoints** | `.omo/checkpoints/<session>.json` every 20 tool calls, on start/finish, around compaction |
| **re-anchor** | one system part after compaction: quotes the task, forbids restarting or inventing work |
| **goal file** | `.omo/goals/<sessionID>.md` on every substantive message: the task, the last four asks verbatim, the additions, the last nudge |
| **one goal** | a message flagged as informational ("у меня поиск запущен, чтобы ты знал") goes to `## Additions` and never replaces the task; an extension of an existing ask replaces it instead of taking another slot; a reverted-and-rewritten message replaces the entry its first version produced, while a second message without a revert is appended |
| **compaction note** | appended as a **new user message** with the user's own words, paths with line ranges, commands, errors, last step, `.omo/state.md` |
| **compaction failure** | silence, not a retry: the cooldown is measured from the failure and doubles 3 → 6 → 12 → 24 → 30 min |
| **emergency mode** | after two failures: above `emergencyRatio` old tool output becomes 600/200 chars, old assistant text and reasoning 600 chars, the last six messages stay byte-identical, and a handoff note carries the goal plus `.omo/state.md` |

The compaction note is a new message on purpose. Adding a text part to a `tool` message makes the
request invalid on strict protocols (`OpenAI Chat: tool messages only support tool-result content
for now`), and appending to an assistant message puts instructions inside the model's own past
output. A fresh trailing user message is legal everywhere.

## The log

`.omo/logs/resilience.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in the project directory. The `at` field is
the event name:

| `at` | when | useful fields |
|---|---|---|
| `setup` | plugin loaded | `plugin` (version), `pid`, `guarded`, `modelSwitching`, option values |
| `compact-backoff` | a compaction failed | `fails`, `emergency`, `nextTryMs` |
| `emergency-trim` | old history was cut because compaction is unavailable | `saved`, `messages`, `used`, `ratio`, `fails` |
| `setup-duplicate` | a simultaneous second load of the same plugin for this root | `plugin`, `pid`, `note` — hooks stay registered once |
| `ctx` | first 12 requests only | `used`, `est`, `cal`, `ratio`, `msgs`, `toolChars` |
| `prune` | tool output elided | `saved`, `messages`, `forced` |
| `calibrate` | a real sample was accepted | `real`, `estimate`, `cal`, `n`, `jump` |
| `compact-request` / `compact-admitted` / `compact-error` | compaction lifecycle | `used`, `error`, `empty` |
| `compact-skip` | trigger fired but was skipped | `why` = `below-keep-window` \| `no-history` |
| `compacting-watchdog` | a `started` event never arrived | `ageMs` |
| `compaction-note` | note appended | `injected`, `state`, `target` |
| `warn` / `warn-rearm` | level entered / log re-armed after a drop | `key`, `ratio`, `mode` |
| `note-strip` | a stale pressure note was removed | `removed` |
| `anchor` | post-compaction re-anchor injected | `task` |
| `goal-addition` | a message was classified as context, not a task (or an early addition was promoted once a task existed) | `chars`, `additions`, `reason` |
| `goal-revision` | a reverted message was rewritten and replaced the entry its first version produced | `kind`, `chars` |
| `retry*` | `retry-hook`, `retry`, `retry-fatal`, `retry-giveup` | `status`, `reason`, `delay`, `budget` |
| `transport-fail` | stream died mid-flight | `count`, `status` |
| `resume*` | `resume`, `resume-sent`, `resume-skip`, `resume-capped` | `reason` |
| `stall*` | `stall`, `stall-skip`, `stall-resolved` | `idleMs`, `status` |
| `checkpoint` | checkpoint written | `reason` |

A healthy long session looks like: steady `calibrate` lines with `cal` between 0.9 and 1.4, one
`warn` per level climb, `compact-request` around 263 500, `compaction-note`, then
`compact-admitted`.

**Is the version I installed the version that is running?** Look at the `setup` line:

```json
{"at":"setup","plugin":"1.8.1","pid":17136,"guarded":"flash1047/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free", ...}
```

A `setup` line **without** `plugin` is a different build still held in memory. The runtime re-reads the
plugin when it starts a server instance for a project, which usually happens on its own (a new
`setup` line with the new version appears after the file changes); if it still shows the old
version, quit the app completely and reopen it. No `setup` line for your session at all is the other,
more common case: the session is not on `flash1047/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, so the plugin is doing
exactly what it promises — nothing.

**Can I use it with a different model?**
The provider block is specific to `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` and the plugin is scoped to
`flash1047/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`. Point it at something else and it does nothing — by design.

**Why does output sometimes stop mid-sentence and then continue?**
A dead stream gets retried. The retry is visible in the log as `retry` / `transport-fail`; it is not
a silent answer change.

**Is this safe to run for a whole workday?**
That is what the test suite and the live sessions target: hours of work with compaction, pruning and
retries. The failure modes it cannot remove are the free pool's latency and load.

1. Quit OpenCode.
2. Remove the `flash1047` provider block, the `plugins` entry with `"./plugins/resilience"`, and —

3. Remove `~/.config/opencode/plugins/resilience/` and, if you added it,

## Free-tier note and limits

The endpoint is OpenCode's own free inference gateway. Requests carry
`Authorization: Bearer public` plus the client's `x-opencode-client` header, and the gateway only
accepts them **from inside the OpenCode client** — which is why the provider is added as
`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` instead of being called with curl. Cost stays $0; there is no key to
buy or leak.

Limits worth knowing before you build on it:

- the free pool is shared, so latency and truncation rates vary with load;
- the model is Flash-tier: excellent for mechanical work, weaker on hard reasoning;
- the window is measured, not guaranteed — if the gateway changes, watch `ctx` and `calibrate` lines
  and treat them as the source of truth.

## This release

**v1.8.1 — stable.** One build; nothing about history is needed to use it.

- **Thresholds use the provider's own number, not the estimator.** After every user prompt the
  plugin reads the last completed step's `input + cache.read` from the transcript and treats it as
  the real prompt size, adding only what arrived since. Live case: the estimator said 303k (98%) on
  a 100k turn where the provider reported 207k (68%) — the model was told the context was full and
  stopped working. The estimate is the fallback when no sample can be read.
- **Pressure notes are nudges, not standing orders.** A note is sent once per level and again only
  when the ratio actually rises; reaching a level no longer re-injects it on every request. The hard
  note no longer says "do not start new work in this turn" and no longer promises a compaction the
  plugin does not own — both were obeyed literally by the model while there was plenty of room.
- **One goal file per chat, nothing shared.** Everything is under `.omo/goals/`, named
  `<sessionID>.md`. There is no `latest.md` and no `goal.md`: a shared copy is exactly the thing that
  let two chats read each other's task, so it is gone. The anchor, the additions hints, the resume
  prompt and the post-compaction prompt all point at the session's own file. Existing goals are moved
  there automatically at startup - `goal.<id>.md` from 1.7.0 and the old single `goal.md`, whose
  session is read from its own footer - so a running chat finds its task at the new path instead of
  losing it. Nothing is overwritten: if a destination already exists, the old file is left untouched.
- **One goal.** An informational message ("у меня поиск запущен, просто чтобы ты знал") is context,
  not a task: it goes to `## Additions` in `goal.md` and is quoted after compaction as context that
  must not be swapped for the goal.
- **Context is not evicted.** Up to twelve additions are kept, so a long session does not silently
  lose the note you asked it to remember; when the anchor or the compaction note can only quote the
  last two, they say how many earlier ones are on disk.
- **An early addition is promoted, not mistaken for the task.** If context arrives before any task
  exists it becomes the goal because it is the only intent on record; the first real task then moves
  it to `## Additions` and out of `## Requirements`.
- **Context is labelled once.** The newest addition is also the message that sets the "last
  instruction", so it used to appear under that heading too - where it read like a command. It is
  written once, under `## Additions`, and the last-instruction field says plainly that the addition
  above is context, not an instruction.
- **A message you take back and rewrite replaces itself.** OpenCode admits the edited text as a fresh
  prompt after removing the reverted message from the transcript. If the prompt you sent last is no
  longer in history and the new one is the same kind (task or addition), the old entry is removed
  first, so a full rewrite - different words, different length - does not leave a stale copy beside
  it. A genuinely new message is still appended, because the previous one is still in the transcript.
- **A launch line is status, not a new task.** "я запускаю chck4.cmd" (present tense) is recognised
  the same way as "у меня запущен": it goes to `## Additions` and the audit already in progress stays
  the goal. With an imperative attached ("я запускаю X, он падает - почини") it is a task again.
- **OpenCode owns compaction; the plugin does not summarise on an estimate.** Two token estimators
  disagreed on live sessions (493k estimated vs 178k reported, then 350k vs ~50k), and each
  disagreement cut history early. The plugin now prunes, warns, retries and re-anchors, while the
  runtime compacts using its own real accounting. `ownCompact: true` restores the old behaviour.
  When the plugin does read a real sample, `used` is the reported `input + cache.read` plus the tail,
  and the `ctx` line carries `src: "real" | "est"`.
- **A rewritten requirement replaces the old one.** Extending a demand keeps one entry instead of
  eating another of the four slots; the longest version wins, and a genuinely new demand is appended.
- A compaction failure is no longer retried into a storm: the cooldown is measured from the failure
  and doubles 3 → 6 → 12 → 24 → 30 min.
- After two failures, emergency trim keeps the session working: old tool output and old assistant
  text are cut, the last six messages stay intact, and a handoff note carries the goal and
  `.omo/state.md`.
- The compaction note carries your last four asks verbatim, file paths with line ranges, the exact
  commands and error lines, and forbids paraphrasing your requirements.
- `.omo/goals/<sessionID>.md` keeps the task, those asks, the additions and your last nudge on disk.
- After compaction the session continues by itself instead of waiting for "continue".
- Context pressure asks for full quality and targeted reads, not short answers.
- 148 assertions; the compaction/pruning core live-verified on OpenCode 2.1.3, the goal/additions
  classification verified against a real chat that exhibited the failure, a five-scenario survival
  probe (anchor, note, disk, twelve-slot cap, pre-task promotion) and a replay of the exact two

- README: the paragraph about `compaction.buffer` still said 15 500 (and a 270 000 trigger that
  15 500 does not give); it now describes the shipped 40 000. Added the caveat that the "auto at"
  numbers assume the runtime triggers at `limit - buffer`.

## v1.2.0 – 2026-10-22

Quality defaults for huge, multi-hour tasks. Behaviour is unchanged for anyone who already
passes explicit options; this changes what a fresh install gets.

### Changed

- **Shipped preset is now `quality`** (was `balanced`):
  - `compact: 0.85` (263 500 of 310 000) instead of 0.90;
  - `compaction.buffer: 40000` (runtime auto at 270 000) instead of 15 500;
  - `keep: 32000` and `compaction.keep.tokens: 32000` instead of 24 000;
  - `pruneSoft: 0.70` (217 000) instead of 0.55 (170 500).
- **Plugin `DEFAULTS` match the preset**: `compact 0.85`, `pruneSoft 0.70`. `keep` stays
  15 000 because that is OpenCode's own default when `compaction.keep.tokens` is unset; the
  installers set 32 000 in both places.
- README, INSTALL, `opencode.snippet.jsonc`, `install.ps1`, `install.sh` and
  `scripts/apply-config.js` all emit the quality preset, so a reinstall no longer resets a
  long-session setup back to the balanced numbers.

### Why

- 85% keeps ~46 000 tokens of headroom for a one-shot estimator error; at 90% the same error
  can push a request past the measured 319 123-token ceiling.
- 32 000 verbatim after compaction keeps 8 000 more tokens of real work than 24 000.
- Pruning at 217 000 instead of 170 500 stops discarding file contents while there is still
  plenty of room.

### Verified

- 53/53 regression assertions.
- `apply-config.js` and `install.ps1` merges on throwaway config dirs: original providers and
  foreign plugin entries preserved, correct quality block produced.
- Live setup: `limit 310000, compact 0.85, keep 32000, keepFloor 35000`.

## v1.1.1 – 2026-10-22

Compaction stops fighting itself, the context estimate stops lying on wide text, and the
reasoning variants are proven at the wire, not assumed.

### Fixed

- **Compaction storm (the big one).** If `compaction.keep.tokens` was larger than the plugin's
  `contextLimit * compact`, the plugin asked for compaction below the runtime's keep window,
  OpenCode answered `Nothing to compact yet`, and the old error handler reset the 3-minute
  cooldown to zero. The next request asked again — compaction on every turn, forever. Now:
  - the floor is `max(18 000, keep + 3 000)` and `keep` is an explicit plugin option that must
    match `compaction.keep.tokens`;
  - a `Nothing to compact yet` rejection keeps the cooldown and increments `compactEmpty`;
  - a watchdog clears a `compacting` flag whose `compaction.ended` event never arrives, so a
    lost event cannot disable compaction permanently either.
- **Runtime auto-compaction raced the plugin.** OpenCode's default threshold is
  `limit - max(15%, 16 000)` = 263 500 on a 310K window, i.e. 85%, so the runtime compacted
  before the plugin's 90% trigger. The shipped config sets `compaction.buffer: 15500`
  (runtime auto at 294 500) and `compaction.keep.tokens: 24000`, aligned with `options.keep`.

### Changed

- **Compaction trigger is 90%** (279 000 of 310 000), up from 85%. The runtime keeps the last
  24 000 tokens verbatim and summarises the older ones.
- **Wide-text aware estimator.** ASCII is counted at 3.6 chars/token, Cyrillic/CJK/emoji at
  2.0 chars/token. A single ASCII divisor undercounted Russian prompts by ~45%.
- **Adaptive calibration.** Real usage (`input + cache.read + cache.write`) is learned per
  step; the EMA uses weight 0.65 when the content mix shifts by more than 30% and 0.4
  otherwise, clamped to 0.4–2.5.
- **Richer compaction note.** It now carries files touched (`filePath/path/file/filename/target`),
  the tools used, the last visible assistant step and `.omo/state.md`, in addition to the task
  and tool count. Still appended as a new user message; existing messages are byte-identical.
- **Tests grew from 34 to 53 assertions**, including the exact storm regression, the keep-floor
  contract and the lost-event watchdog.

### Verified

- **Reasoning effort on the wire (OpenCode 2.1.2):** a capturing proxy in front of the provider
  recorded `reasoning_effort: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "max"` for the four variants. 12 runs
  of the same puzzle all answered correctly; `max` had the highest mean reasoning tokens
  (494.7 vs 429.0 low), though the sample is noisy.
- **Forced live compaction:** `contextLimit=20 000`, real usage 48 532, three large reads
  (109 170 tool chars) -> `compact-request` -> `compaction-note` (`user:new`) ->
  `compaction.started` -> `delta` -> `ended` -> post-compaction checkpoint -> `DONE-C`.
- **Isolation:** a run on another provider produced only a `setup` log line and zero session
  events (the provider itself had no balance, which is irrelevant to the scoping result).

## v1.1.0 – 2026-10-22

Boring on purpose: no model switching, no duplicated protocol text, and the task survives every
compaction. This release is about removing ways the plugin could quietly make a session worse.

### Fixed

- **Compaction used to die with `provider.invalid-request`.**
  `OpenAI Chat tool messages only support tool-result content for now` was the visible symptom:
  the compaction hook appended its note to the last message of the request, and when that message
  was a `tool` message the whole request became invalid on strict protocols (OpenAI Chat,
  Anthropic Messages). The note is now appended as a **new user message** and no hook ever
  rewrites an existing message.
- **The first user prompt of a session was never recorded.** The `prompt` hook checked the scope
  before the session model was known, so it returned early — and resume/compaction notes then had
  no task text to preserve. Hooks that can fire before the first request now resolve the model
  first.
- **Pruning marker wording.** It claimed the full output "is on disk", which is not always true.
  It now states plainly that the text was removed client-side and must not be guessed.

### Removed

- **Model failover** (`failover` pool, `switchAfter`, `maxSwitches`, `rateCooldownMs`,
  `deadCooldownMs`, `restoreAfterMs`, `restoreOnNewTurn`, `fallback`, `fallbackAfter`,
  `pickNext`, `switchTo`, `restore-primary`). It silently replaced the model the user picked with
  whatever answered, changing window size, reasoning shape and quality mid-task. It fired 3 times
  in two days of real use. A 429 or 5xx now only changes the backoff; a dead endpoint fails the
  turn and the resume prompt surfaces it.
- **Per-session long-session protocol block.** OpenCode already loads
  `~/.config/opencode/instructions/long-session.md` into the system prompt for every session
  (verified against the instruction blobs in `opencode.db`), so the injected copy only burned
  tokens and drifted from the file.
- **`prune-check` debug logging** (one line per pruning evaluation, ~250 lines in two days).

### Added

- **Post-compaction re-anchor.** The first request after a successful compaction gets one system
  part quoting the user's task verbatim: continue from `.omo/state.md`, do not restart, do not ask
  the user to repeat anything, do not invent new work.
- **Recent tool trace** in the compaction note (last 6 tool names), so the summary keeps what the
  agent actually did, not just a count.
- **Resume prompt quotes the task** (`Your task, verbatim from the user: "..."`), so a resumed
  turn cannot drift into a different job.
- **Hard scope.** The plugin is guarded to `flash1047/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` by default (both
  provider and model id), so dropping the config options cannot widen it to every model.
- **`test/resilience.test.mjs`** — 34 assertions, no dependencies, run with
  `node --experimental-strip-types test/resilience.test.mjs`. It drives the plugin through a fake
  session and a fake event stream, including the exact message shape that broke compaction.

## v1.0.0

Initial release: tool-output pruning, proactive compaction, compaction note, checkpoints, retry
policy, auto-resume, stall detection, model failover, protocol block.

# INSTALL — procedure for an AI assistant

> Human? Use [`README.md`](README.md) — it has a 60-second quick start. This file is the same
> procedure written for an agent that is asked to "install this model".

You are installing a model entry + plugin into **OpenCode 2.x** on the user's machine.
Follow the steps exactly. Do not invent files that are not listed here.
Everything you need is inside this repository.

## 0. Locate the OpenCode config directory

- Windows: `C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode` (i.e. `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode`)
- macOS / Linux: `~/.config/opencode`

The config file is `opencode.jsonc` or `opencode.json` in that directory.
If neither exists, create `opencode.json`.

## 1. Copy the plugin

Copy:

```
plugin/resilience/index.ts
```

to:

```
<config-dir>/plugins/resilience/index.ts
```

Create the `plugins/resilience` directory if needed. The plugin MUST be a directory that
contains `index.ts` — a flat `resilience.ts` file is not loaded by OpenCode 2.x.

## 1b. Copy the long-session rules

Copy:

```
instructions/long-session.md
```

to:

```
<config-dir>/instructions/long-session.md
```

Do not overwrite the destination if it already exists and differs: the user may have edited it.

## 2. Merge this into the config file

Add the `flash1047` key inside the top-level `provider` object, the plugin entry inside the
top-level `plugins` array, the rules file inside the top-level `instructions` array, and tune
the top-level `compaction` object. Keep everything else that is already in the file.

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "flash1047": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "flash 1047",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1",
        "apiKey": "public"
      },
      "models": {
        "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free": {
          "name": "flash 1047 - Super Free",
          "limit": { "context": 310000, "output": 32000 },
          "capabilities": {
            "tools": true,
            "reasoning": true,
            "input": ["text", "image"],
            "output": ["text"],
            "temperature": true
          },
          "cost": { "input": 0, "output": 0 },
          "variants": {
            "low": { "reasoningEffort": "low" },
            "medium": { "reasoningEffort": "medium" },
            "high": { "reasoningEffort": "high" },
            "max": { "reasoningEffort": "max" }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "compaction": {
    "auto": true,
    "keep": { "tokens": 32000 },
    "buffer": 40000
  },
  "instructions": ["~/.config/opencode/instructions/long-session.md"],
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "./plugins/resilience",
      "options": {
        "onlyProviderID": "flash1047",
        "onlyModelID": "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free",
        "contextLimit": 310000,
        "keep": 32000,
        "warn": 0.7,
        "compact": 0.85,
        "pruneSoft": 0.7,
        "hard": 0.93,
        "every": 20,
        "stallMs": 900000,
        "maxResumes": 4,
        "resumeCooldownMs": 120000
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- The model **key** must stay `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` — that string is sent upstream as the
  model name. Only `name` is cosmetic.
- Do not remove or modify the existing `opencode` provider. The point is to have both models.
- The `instructions` entry must be a `~/` or absolute path (relative entries are searched from
  the workspace upward, not from the config directory). If `instructions` already contains an
  entry ending in `long-session.md`, do not add a second one. Keep the user's other entries.
- If `plugins` already contains an entry whose `package` is `./plugins/resilience`, replace
  that entry instead of adding a duplicate.
- Back up the config first (`opencode.jsonc.bak`) — editing JSONC by machine can drop comments.
- **`contextLimit` must equal `limit.context`** (310 000). **`options.keep` must equal
  `compaction.keep.tokens`** (32 000). Both mismatches cause constant compaction:
  the plugin asks below the runtime's keep window and gets `Nothing to compact yet`.
- **`compaction.buffer` must be 40 000.** Without it OpenCode auto-compacts at
  `310000 - max(15%, 16000) = 263500`, exactly at the plugin's trigger. With the buffer the
  runtime fires at 270 000, above the plugin and below the measured 319K ceiling.
- Do not lower `buffer` below 40 000 and do not raise `compact` above 0.85 without re-measuring.

Prefer the automated merge if Node.js is available:

```bash
node scripts/apply-config.js
```

It finds the config, backs it up, merges all four blocks (provider, compaction, plugins,
instructions) idempotently and copies the plugin and the rules file.

## 3. Restart OpenCode

Quit it completely (Windows: tray icon -> Quit; do not just close the window) and start it
again. The plugin, providers and compaction settings load at startup.

## 4. Verify

1. The model picker shows **flash 1047 - Super Free** with provider `flash1047`, next to the
   original **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free**.
2. Send any short prompt to the new model; it answers normally.
3. In the project directory, `.omo/logs/resilience.jsonl` contains a line with `"at":"setup"`,
   `"limit":310000`, `"compact":0.85`, `"keep":32000` and `"keepFloor":35000`.
4. Send a prompt to the **original** model and confirm no new lines appear in that log file for
   that session — the plugin is scoped to the new provider only.
5. If the user has an existing long session, confirm compaction happens at ~85%, not every
   turn. The log shows `compact-request` with `used` close to 263 500; a `compact-error`
   containing `Nothing to compact yet` means `keep` and `compaction.keep.tokens` disagree.

If step 4 fails, the plugin is loaded but the scope options are missing: re-check
`plugins[].options.onlyProviderID` and `onlyModelID`.

## 5. Optional: sanity-check the context window

OpenCode passes `limit.context` to the client-side budget. 310 000 was measured safe against
the free gateway (319 123 accepted, 325 760 rejected). If the user reports
`400 context_length_exceeded`, lower `limit.context`, `options.contextLimit` and
`compaction.buffer` together — keep `limit.context - buffer` above the plugin trigger
(`compact * limit.context`) and below 319 000.

# Long-session rules

These rules apply to long tasks: hours of work, many tool calls, large projects. They are short on
purpose, because this file is sent with every request.

1. **State file.** Keep `.omo/state.md` current: the user's goal, decisions already made, files
   changed, what is done, and the next unfinished step. Update it after each meaningful milestone,
   not at the end. Facts only, no narration.
2. **Compaction.** The history can be compacted at any time. After a compaction, continue from the
   summary and `.omo/state.md`. Do not restart the task, do not ask the user again for anything
   already answered, and do not invent new work.
3. **Reading.** Do not re-read a whole large file you have already read. Use grep, or read ranges
   with offset and limit. If a tool output says text was removed by `[omni-resilience]`, that text
   is gone from your context: run the tool again with a narrower query and never guess the missing
   part.
4. **Automatic notes.** A message that starts with `[omni-resilience]` is an automatic note from the
   client, not from the user. Follow it, then keep working on the user's task.
5. **Verification.** Before you say a step is done, run the check that proves it (tests, build, type
   check, a quick run). Report what you verified and what you could not verify.
6. **Scope.** Do exactly the task that was asked. List unrelated problems you notice in
   `.omo/state.md` under "Found, not fixed" instead of fixing them silently.
